title: Critical perspectives
examples: How does a feminist reading change how we see this poem?
Can you explain the Marxist view when looking at class struggle in a novel?
What does 'postcolonial' mean when we analyze literature from a former colony?

explain.say: Today we will look at three ways to read literature. These are called critical perspectives. Each lens helps us see different meanings in a text.

The feminist lens focuses on gender roles and power dynamics. It questions how literature treats women's experiences. For example, it might examine how a character is limited by societal expectations.
The Marxist lens looks at economic structures and class struggle. It suggests that money and social class drive the action. Consider a story where wealth creates a clear divide between people.
The postcolonial lens examines the lasting effects of colonialism. It looks at the relationship between colonizers and colonized peoples. Think about texts dealing with empire or cultural identity.

In everyday life, you can use these lenses to view advertisements. A feminist reading might question who is portrayed as desirable. A Marxist reading could question who can afford the advertised product.

items: Marxist: Who can afford this lifestyle?
Postcolonial: Whose culture is being marketed?

explain.say: A common mistake is applying only one lens to a complex text. Literature is rich because multiple perspectives can overlap. Always try to see how these ideas interact with each other.

faq.q: What is the main difference between feminist and Marxist criticism?
faq.a: Feminist criticism focuses on gender inequality and representation. Marxist criticism focuses on economic inequality and class power.
asks: Does feminism only talk about women?
Is class struggle the same as gender struggle?

faq.q: When do I use the postcolonial lens?
faq.a: You use it when the text deals with cultures that were once controlled by another power. It looks at resistance to that power.
asks: Does this apply to modern politics?
Is it only for books set in Africa or Asia?

faq.q: Can I use all three lenses on the same novel?
faq.a: Yes, you can. Analyzing a text through multiple lenses shows a very deep and complex understanding of the material.
asks: Will my essay be confusing if I use three theories?
Is it okay to mix theories?

faq.q: Are these theories always about politics?
faq.a: No, they can be applied to personal relationships and social structures too. They are tools for analyzing power in any context.
asks: Can I use this for poetry?
Does it have to be a big historical event?

faq.a: Agency refers to a character's ability to act independently and make free choices. The lens examines when characters lose or gain this ability.
asks: What does it mean to have agency?

facts: Feminist criticism analyzes how literature portrays gender roles and power.
Marxist criticism views literature through the lens of economic class struggle.
Postcolonial criticism examines the cultural and political effects of imperialism.
These lenses are critical tools, not absolute truths about a text.

quiz.say: A novel shows a poor family struggling against a wealthy factory owner. Which lens is most appropriate?
quiz.why: The focus on wealth and the factory owner points directly to class conflict.

wrong.1: This lens focuses on gender roles, not the owner's wealth.
wrong.2: This lens requires a history of foreign control or empire.
wrong.3: The situation clearly demonstrates an economic imbalance.

quiz.say: A poem critiques how society expects women to behave. Which lens is best suited for this analysis?
quiz.why: The core subject is the restriction of women's roles by society.

wrong.0: While class can affect women, the primary focus here is gender.
wrong.1: There is no mention of foreign occupation or empire.
wrong.2: The critique is specifically about gender expectations.

quiz.say: A story features characters from a formerly colonized nation interacting with former colonizers. Which perspective should you use?
quiz.why: The relationship between former rulers and ruled peoples is the key element.

wrong.0: This lens would only be useful if gender was the main conflict.
wrong.1: While economics are involved, the historical power dynamic is key.
wrong.2: The specific historical context of empire demands this lens.
